meta.title: Tideline Sail Trim Knowledge Base
meta.scope: Upwind/downwind trim rules for small and mid-size keelboats (fractional and masthead), coachable in one sentence.
meta.conventions: TWS true wind speed kt; TWA true wind angle deg; speeds kn. 'coachLine' is a suggested spoken cue. Confidence: high = directly stated in a sailmaker/class guide or real polar; medium = synthesised across sources; low = estimate.

windBands.goal: Power and flow, not height: full sails, open leeches, build speed before you point.

main.outhaul: Eased a few inches (J/105: 'ease a few inches'; ILCA ~10-15 cm off the boom at max depth) for a deep, powerful foot.
main.cunningham: Off; small scallops/wrinkles at the luff are fine.
main.backstay: Fully off (J/24 'none' 0-6 kt; J/70 'fully slack' in light VMG mode). Headstay sag powers the jib.
main.traveler: Car to windward / all the way up so the boom sits on or just above centerline (J/24 'all the way up'; J/105 'boom on centerline or slightly above').
main.sheet: Eased enough that ALL leech telltales fly; top batten roughly parallel to boom or slightly open. Over-sheeting stalls the leech and kills acceleration.
main.coachLine: Ease the main until all the leech telltales are flying; in this breeze twist is speed.

jib.lead: Neutral or a touch forward for depth (Etchells: up to 3/4" forward for power; J/24 genoa 1 hole aft of neutral in flat water, on neutral in chop).
jib.halyard: Soft: small wrinkles/scallops along the luff ('too loose is better than too tight' - J/24 guide).
jib.sheet: Eased off the spreader (J/24 genoa 3-4" off in flat water, 3-6" in chop; J/105 jib to spreader tip). Leech should not hook to windward.
jib.coachLine: Ease the jib an inch - let the leech breathe and build speed first.

windBands.helm: Steer gently with minimal rudder; sail slightly lower (footing) to keep leeward telltales streaming; keep the inside jib telltale 'nervous' rather than lifting. Don't pinch - height comes from flow over the keel.
windBands.crew: Weight forward and to leeward for a little leeward heel (helps sails fall into shape, reduces wetted surface); sit still. J/105: two crew forward of shrouds to leeward.
windBands.telltales: All main leech telltales streaming; jib inside telltale just ticking, outside always streaming. If the bottom outside jib telltale stalls constantly you are over-trimmed - ease.

windBands.goal: Full power with the least twist: point and go. This is the band where height pays.

main.outhaul: Moving toward the band/clew mark as breeze builds; flatten the foot once crew is hiking.
main.cunningham: Off or just enough to remove big wrinkles until ~10-12 kt (J/24: none until ~12 kt).
main.backstay: Light to 1/4 on (J/24 7-12 kt '1/4 on'); use it to control headstay sag and flatten the top as you become fully powered.
main.vang: Take the slack out at ~8 kt and snug as you approach overpowered (J/24 8-15 kt 'remove all slack'; J/105 speed guide 'snug the vang' at 8 kt).
main.traveler: Car up until the crew is on the rail, then centre the boom; don't drop the boom below centerline yet - play the traveler for heel (J/105: 'play the traveler aggressively ... don't drop it below centerline').
main.sheet: Trim hard enough that the top leech telltale stalls roughly 40-60% of the time (J/24: flies 50-60% of the time up to 10 kt; J/105: stall top telltale ~60% at 8 kt). Top batten parallel to the boom; in flat water it may poke slightly to windward.
main.coachLine: Sheet on until the top telltale is hiding about half the time - top batten parallel to the boom.

jib.lead: Neutral; in chop 1-2 holes forward (J/24 7-13 kt choppy). Lead so the luff breaks evenly top to bottom (top inside slightly first is OK).
jib.halyard: Just smooth in flat water; small wrinkles OK in chop for a rounder entry and wider groove.
jib.sheet: Close to the spreader (J/24 genoa 2-3" off in flat, 2-4" in chop; J/105 jib 6-9" inside spreader tip). Never tighter than ~1" off the spreader.
jib.coachLine: Bring the jib in to about two inches off the spreader and lock it - now steer to the telltales.

windBands.helm: Steer to the jib telltales in the groove: head up until the inside just lifts, bear away slightly. Small rudder angles; a few degrees of weather helm is ideal. Two modes - speed (leech telltales flying) and height (upper leech telltales stalled).
windBands.crew: Move weight to weather and hike as the breeze reaches ~8-10 kt; stack together just behind the shrouds at max beam; keep heel constant.
windBands.telltales: Jib: outside streaming, inside on the edge of lifting. Main: top leech telltale stalling ~half the time; if it never flies you are overtrimmed.

windBands.goal: Control heel and helm while keeping the leeches working: flatten first, then twist.

main.outhaul: To the band/max (Quantum expert: 'needs to go all the way to band' in strong wind).
main.cunningham: On - remove luff wrinkles and then pull past smooth to keep draft forward as backstay bends the mast.
main.backstay: 1/2 to 3/4 on (J/24 12-18 kt); Melges 24 ~75% on from 12 kt. Play it with each puff on fractional rigs.
main.vang: Firm - enough that the boom doesn't rise when the sheet is eased (J/24: above 15 kt 'tension hard enough that the boom doesn't rise').
main.traveler: Traveler to middle / leeward and play it hard: down in puffs, up in lulls. Ease traveler before sheet when a puff hits to keep the leech working.
main.sheet: Top batten parallel to open ~3 deg; top leech telltale flying most of the time. Use sheet/traveler to hold a steady heel.
main.coachLine: Puff coming - traveler down, keep her on her feet; bring it back up as it passes.

jib.lead: Move aft to open (twist) the upper leech (J/105 speed guide: 'lead further aft' in puffs); in chop keep 1-2 holes forward of flat-water position to retain power low.
jib.sheet: Ease slightly off the spreader (J/24 genoa 4-6" off at 14-18 kt choppy; J/105 back to ~3" inside tip at 18+). Ease ~1/2" and foot a little for lift as it builds (Melges 24).
jib.coachLine: Ease the jib half an inch and foot a degree - we need speed, not height, in these puffs.

windBands.helm: Hold a constant heel: feather up slightly in puffs (let the inside telltales dance), foot in lulls. Avoid big rudder angles; if the helm loads up, the trimmer depowers.
windBands.crew: Max hike, consistent, weight together at max beam; slide aft a little as waves build.
windBands.telltales: Inside jib telltales may lift in puffs while feathering - acceptable. Main leech telltales stream constantly; use heel and helm, not telltales, as the main guide.

windBands.goal: Survive and go fast: flattest sails, open leeches, smallest heel and rudder angle; depower in sequence, reef/change down before you're out of controls.

main.vang: Hard (keeps leech controlled when you dump sheet), but on some boats ease slightly to twist the top more (J/70 heavy: 'less vang and a twistier main').
main.traveler: Below centerline (J/24 2-3" below) or dumped in puffs; the main may luff/bubble forward - that's OK.
main.sheet: Top batten open 3-6 deg (J/24); play it continuously.
main.coachLine: Everything on - backstay, cunningham, outhaul - and dump the traveler in the puffs; a back-winded main is fine, a rounded-up boat isn't.

jib.lead: On or aft of neutral to twist off the top (J/24 18+ on neutral in chop).
jib.halyard: Tight - draft forward ('pull past removing wrinkles' J/105).
jib.sheet: Further off the spreader (J/24 genoa 6-8"); J/105 jib ~3" inside spreader tip.
jib.coachLine: Halyard up hard and lead aft - twist the top of the jib open.

windBands.helm: Feather in puffs, never fight the helm; heel should be held at the boat's target (First 36.7 targets show ~22-23 deg as max useful; most small keelboats faster flatter).
windBands.crew: Everyone hiking hard, weight aft in waves; consider smaller headsail/reef on cruiser-racers when depowering controls are maxed.
windBands.telltales: Ignore jib telltales in gusts; sail by heel angle and helm load ('feather, don't fight').

order: 7. Reef or change to smaller headsail
depowerSequence.rule: Flatten first (keeps closed leeches and pointing), then twist - especially in chop. Flatten in smooth water, twist in waves.
depowerSequence.confidence: medium (order synthesised; class guides differ - e.g. some keep rake fixed, some ease vang)

seaState.when: Short steep waves (wind against current, short fetch, motorboat chop, waves on the bow).
adjust: More power and twist: 'Always add depth when you're twisting the sails' - ease backstay a little, ease outhaul to deepen the bottom.
Traveler up to windward, ease mainsheet to open the top leech.
Jib lead forward 1-2 holes (inch or two) and ease jib sheet; add inhaul if you have it.
Slightly softer/wrinkled jib halyard for a rounder entry and wider groove (J/105).
Foot off a few degrees for punch until the outside telltales dance; don't feather up in fresh breeze in chop.
Don't steer up waves and bear off down them - let a well-trimmed boat find its path; trimmer plays traveler/sheet rather than helm steering.
Crew aft a little in big waves; keep weight together to limit pitching.
seaState.coachLine: We're stopping in the chop - foot two degrees, ease the backstay and twist the main a touch.
cues: Stopping in a wave and slow to re-accelerate -> more twist + depth
Masthead swinging a lot -> lots of depth and twist
Sail breaks at the top as the mast pitches forward -> too full/too twisted

seaState.when: Smooth water (sheltered, lee of land, steady breeze).
adjust: Less twist, straight leeches on main and jib: sheet harder, traveler down a bit, backstay tighter.
Flatter sails for less drag; jib lead back to flat-water position (J/24: 1 aft of neutral in light flat water).
Slightly looser jib halyard (small wrinkles low) for pointing (J/105).
Height mode pays: top main leech telltale can stall most of the time in medium flat water.
Depower by flattening rather than twisting.
seaState.coachLine: Flat water - trim for height, top telltale stalled, squeeze up a degree.

seaState.when: Long, larger waves with relatively flat faces (ocean swell, long fetch).
adjust: Moderate depth and twist - between flat and chop modes; long waves allow a flatter setup than chop.
Steer actively over big waves: up slightly on the face, bear off over the crest (J/70: choose mode per tack based on wave angle).
When waves hit from the side, carry a bit more helm so you aren't pushed to leeward; sheet the main more and leave the jib.
Downwind: use waves to surf - bear off down the face, heat up in troughs; crew aft to keep the bow out.
seaState.coachLine: Long waves - steer up the face, bear off over the top, keep speed on.
seaState.confidence: medium (swell-specific guidance is thinner in sources; partly inferred from chop/flat rules)

seaState.when: Waves on the bow on one tack, from the side on the other.
adjust: Bow-down mode on the wave tack: traveler centred, backstay/vang to inversion wrinkles, play sheet for steady heel, hit target speed before pointing.
Height mode on the beam-sea tack: traveler 1/3-1/2 up, less inhaul, ease main to stay flat (J/70).
seaState.coachLine: Change gears on this tack - waves are on the bow now, go to bow-down mode.

telltales.fix: Bear away slightly or trim the jib in a bit; in a lull briefly overtrim then ease as you bear off.
telltales.coachLine: Inside telltale's lifting - bear off a hair.

telltales.symptom: Leeward (outside) jib telltale stalling/drooping or spinning
telltales.fix: Head up, or ease the jib - you're too low or over-trimmed. In a puff, ease then re-trim as helm settles.
telltales.coachLine: Outside telltale is stalled - come up or ease an inch.

telltales.fix: Sheet is too tight (no flow around the sail) - ease slowly until both stream.
telltales.coachLine: Jib is choked - ease it until the telltales come alive.

telltales.symptom: Inside and outside jib telltales break at the same time
telltales.fix: Groove too narrow - ease the jib about an inch.
telltales.coachLine: Groove's too tight - ease an inch.

telltales.symptom: Top inside jib telltale lifts well before the bottom
telltales.fix: Top is too twisted: move the lead forward (a little top-first break is OK; lead slightly aft is the safer error).
telltales.coachLine: Top's breaking early - lead forward a hole.

telltales.symptom: Bottom inside jib telltale lifts before the top
telltales.fix: Lead too far forward (foot too full, top too closed) - move the lead aft.
telltales.coachLine: Bottom's breaking first - lead back a hole.

telltales.symptom: Top main leech telltale stalled all the time (light air)
telltales.fix: Over-sheeted or too much vang - ease sheet until it flies; in light air all leech telltales should fly.
telltales.coachLine: Main leech is closed - ease the sheet till the top telltale flies.

telltales.symptom: Top main leech telltale never stalls (medium air)
telltales.fix: Leech too open, leaking power - trim sheet (or vang) until it stalls ~half the time; UK Sailmakers tip: trim to the stall then ease until it flows ~95% for cruising mode.
telltales.coachLine: Main's too open - give me a little more sheet.

telltales.fix: Badly over-trimmed - ease sheet, raise traveler to keep boom near centre with more twist.

telltales.symptom: Jib leech telltale (non-overlapping jib, top 25%) stalling
telltales.fix: Too hard or lead too low/forward - ease or move lead aft so it keeps flying.
telltales.coachLine: Jib leech is stalling - ease or lead aft.

telltales.symptom: Heavy air: telltales unreadable/constantly lifting in puffs
telltales.fix: Stop chasing them - sail by heel and helm; feather in puffs, foot in lulls.
telltales.coachLine: Forget the telltales - hold the heel.

fixes: Ease the traveler down (before the sheet) in puffs - keeps the leech working.
Reduce heel: hike harder, flatten the main (outhaul, cunningham, backstay).
Add twist to the main (ease sheet a little) - J/105 guide: 'too much helm and slow -> add twist'.
Move jib lead aft only if the jib is not the cause; ensure jib is not under-trimmed.
Long-term: reduce mast rake (rake forward) if it's on both tacks in all conditions.
symptoms.coachLine: She's loading up - drop the traveler and get her flatter.

symptoms.symptom: Lee helm / neutral-dead helm in light air
fixes: Trim main a touch / traveler up to bring the boom to centre.
A little leeward heel (crew to leeward).
Long-term: more aft rake (J/70: adjust rake until helm is balanced; Etchells: base +1/4" in light air).
symptoms.coachLine: No feel in the helm - traveler up and get a little heel.

symptoms.symptom: Boat feels slow/sticky (sluggish, telltales flowing, helm dead)
fixes: Bear off 2-3 degrees to rebuild speed before pointing.
Add power: traveler up, ease backstay/outhaul/halyards, jib lead forward.
Ease the jib a couple of inches - an over-trimmed jib narrows the groove.
Check for weed/dirty bottom (Catalina 27 owners: a clean hull 'really affects pointing').
symptoms.coachLine: We're sticky - foot two degrees and ease the jib an inch until we're at target.

fixes: Reduce twist: more mainsheet/vang, jib lead slightly forward or sheet in (J/105: 'lacks height -> reduce twist').
Tighten backstay to cut headstay sag (in medium air).
Traveler up so the boom is on centerline.
Make sure you are up to target speed first, then squeeze up a degree at a time.
Flat water: switch to height mode (top leech telltales stalled).
symptoms.coachLine: We're at speed - trim the main a click and squeeze up a degree.

fixes: Bear away until the outside jib telltales stream and speed returns.
Ease jib slightly; add a touch of twist.
Target the polar VMG angle, not the tightest angle - best VMG is rarely the closest angle.
symptoms.coachLine: We're pinching - foot off and get back to target.

fixes: Hike / move crew to max beam.
Depower in sequence: outhaul, cunningham, backstay, traveler down, ease sheet.
Feather in puffs.
Reef or smaller headsail when controls are maxed (Catalina 27: deep main reef before going smaller on headsail).
symptoms.coachLine: Too much heel - traveler down, everyone hike, feather the puffs.

fixes: Exit a few degrees low of close-hauled (wider in light air and big seas).
Jib a few inches short of full trim, trimming in as speed builds (Melges 24: ~90% then finish after hiking).
Main: ease sheet, traveler up, backstay off for depth, then re-trim at speed.
Crew still/hiking until the boat is back at target - no spinnaker prep.
symptoms.coachLine: Out of the tack - foot for speed, jib not all the way in yet... now trim.

fixes: Crew together, near max beam; move slightly aft in big waves.
Bear off a few degrees for punch; add depth + twist.
symptoms.coachLine: We're pitching - stack together and foot a little.

symptoms.symptom: Hard to stay in the groove
fixes: Add twist to widen the groove (ease main, lead aft).
Ease the jib a couple inches.
Rounder jib entry: soften halyard a touch in chop.
symptoms.coachLine: Groove's too narrow - ease the jib an inch and give me a little twist.

fixes: Build speed before pointing - keels need flow (Melges 24: keep >= 2.5 kt at the start).
Ease sheets slightly and foot.
symptoms.coachLine: We're sliding - foot and build speed.

general.rule: Sail the polar VMG angle; deeper in medium air, hotter in light air and when planing is possible.
general.coachLine: Heat up 5 degrees to get the kite drawing, then soak in the puff.

general.rule: Puffs: bear away (soak) with the pressure; lulls: head up to keep apparent wind and speed. Don't overheat in lulls or soak too far in puffs - scallop gently.
general.coachLine: Puff - bear off with it; lull - come up and keep her moving.

general.rule: Spinnaker sheet: ease until a slight curl appears in the luff, then trim just enough to stop it collapsing ('if in doubt, ease it out').
general.coachLine: Ease till it curls, then a tiny trim.

general.rule: Main downwind: fully out, vang so the top batten is parallel to the boom (J/24, J/105 heavy); slightly open (~5 deg) in light air.
general.coachLine: Vang it so the top batten is parallel to the boom.

general.rule: Backstay off downwind (J/105: ease fully before bearing away) on most boats - but J/70 keeps it on hard in strong breeze for kite luff tension.

Heel: light air slight leeward heel (crew to leeward/forward); medium-heavy flat or slight windward heel to rotate the kite to windward and sail lower (J/105 up to ~10 deg windward heel in heavy air).
Crew forward in light air (lift transom), aft as speed builds and when surfing/planing.

asymmetric.rule: Ease the tack line in medium air so the luff rotates to windward and you can sail deeper; tighten it toward the sprit in light air and when control is an issue (J/70: ease tack line 4-5" in medium unless very choppy).
If the kite collapses, don't just trim harder - helm heads up slightly while the trimmer trims in steadily.
Practical depth limit for a sprit A-sail ~165 deg TWA in 12 kt; 170 usually precedes a collapse.
Planing boats: in planing breeze sail a couple of degrees higher to get on the plane, then hold it (Melges 24 planes ~14 kt TWS).
Gybe: match the kite gybe to the helm's turn rate; light air: gybe the kite first, then the main; heavy air: get the main across at full speed.

symmetric.rule: Pole height: set so the luff breaks evenly / curl starts mid-luff. Breaks high -> raise pole; breaks low -> lower pole ('move the pole to the break').
symmetric.coachLine: Luff's breaking high - pole up an inch.

symmetric.rule: Pole fore/aft: guy so the pole is ~perpendicular to the apparent wind; mid-seam vertical. Rolling usually means the pole is too far aft - ease it forward.
Keep inboard and outboard pole ends level (pole perpendicular to mast). Raising pole: ease sheet and guy; lowering: trim both ('down and in, up and out').
Heavy air deep sailing: twing down on the sheet to keep the clew low; don't over-square the pole; keep the clew forward of the headstay.

planingThresholds.J/70: surfing 12-13 kt, lazy planing 14-15 kt, weight aft 17-18 kt

wipeoutRecovery.rule: Ease vang, mainsheet and spinnaker together; J/70: release vang and drop kite halyard ~8 ft if wiped out; Melges 24: backwind jib, ease vang.

targets.derivation: Boat speed = VMG / cos(TWA) from certificate 'Beat VMG/Beat Angles' and 'Run VMG/Gybe Angles'.
targets.notes: Planing sportboat; downwind 20 kt is planing (VMG 9.13). LWL approximate (not on certificate).
targets.confidence: high (VPP prediction - real boats with good crews typically sail within ~95-102% of these; calibrate instruments)

targets.sourceType: ORC VPP via Keel Index (median-GPH of 51 ORC certificates)
targets.notes: Only 14 kt angles published; other-wind boat speeds use assumed angles (43/39/39 deg) - mark estimatedUpwind as medium confidence. 8/12/16 kt not published: interpolate.
targets.confidence: high for VMG; medium for derived boat speeds

targets.sourceType: Quantum Sails tuning guide target table (true wind)
targets.notes: Also gives apparent-wind targets (AWA ~25-26 deg upwind 6-16 kt). Heel targets useful for coaching: ~10 deg at 8 kt, ~18 deg at 12 kt, 22 deg at 16-20 kt.

targets.sourceType: ESTIMATE - no published polar found (Keel Index has none; ORC has no C27 class file)
targets.method: Upwind = fraction x hull speed (1.34*sqrt(21.75)=6.25 kn). Fractions taken slightly below those of the ORC one-design polars here because the C27 is heavier (D/L ~297, PHRF ~204-207 vs J/24 ~170) and usually toe-rail sheeted (owners report it won't tack through 90 deg). Downwind assumes symmetric spinnaker, scaled from J/24 ORC run speeds by ~0.95-1.0 (longer LWL offsets weight).
targets.notes: Owners' advice: sail flat ('less heel is better'), keep a big headsail up, genoa ~2" off the spreader above 10 kt, foot for speed rather than pinch, clean bottom. Replace these numbers with the boat's own logged data after a few races.

targets.formula: upwindTarget(TWS) = f(TWS) * 1.34 * sqrt(LWL_ft); twaUp ~ 43-45 deg @6 kt, ~41-42 @8, ~39-40 @10, ~38-39 @12-16, opening ~1-2 deg at 20 kt (heavier/older boats +2-4 deg).
targets.f_upwind_note: f_upwind = light one-design sportboat/keelboat curve (ORC). For heavier cruiser-racers use f_upwind_cruiserRacer.
targets.downwindTwa: Symmetric kite: ~145-150 @6 kt, ~150-155 @10, ~160-180 @12+. Asymmetric/sprit: ~140-145 @6, ~148-152 @10, ~140-150 in planing breeze (heat up to plane).
caveats: Derived from ORC VPP polars of light 20-ft-LWL one-designs; fractions are lower for heavy cruisers (subtract ~0.03-0.06) and for boats with old sails/dirty bottoms.
LWL values used for one-designs are approximate (not on certificates), so f values carry ~+/-3% error.
Use only until the app has logged the user's own speeds; then build a personal polar (95th percentile of steady-state samples per TWS/TWA bin).
It is a soft limit for displacement hulls, not a wall; heavy boats rarely exceed ~1.2-1.3 x sqrt(LWL) upwind.

Upwind targets sit at ~0.71 of hull speed at 6 kt TWS and ~0.96-0.97 at 12-16 kt for light one-designs (ORC polars), but only ~0.64 / ~0.85-0.87 for a cruiser-racer like the First 36.7 (Quantum targets).

Planing/surfing boats (J/70, Melges 24, J/80 downwind) exceed it routinely: ORC predicts J/70 12.6 kn at 135 deg/20 kt and Melges 24 13.3 kn - ~2x hull speed. Never cap targets at hull speed downwind for these boats.
Effective LWL grows with heel and overhangs (older boats like the Catalina 27 gain a little).

coachingPrinciples.rule: Speed first, then height: get to target speed before squeezing up.
Make trim changes in building breeze, never as the breeze fades.
Keep heel constant; in moderate-heavy air heel is the primary steering guide.
More twist = less power, wider groove, more forgiveness; less twist = more power and pointing. Light air: twist; medium: least twist; heavy: add twist.
Deep sails for chop/light air/acceleration; flat sails for smooth water and heavy air.
Mark and record settings (halyard, jib car, sheet, backstay) so fast settings are repeatable.
Upwind modes: cruising (~90% of the time), height (flat water, top leech telltales stalled), speed/fast-forward (waves, tactics: twist off, more depth, foot).
